name: @plexui/ui
description: The most flexible UI kit for React. Production-grade components, design tokens and a 9-size scale that AI agents use correctly.

setup.provider: Wrap your app with <PlexUIProvider linkComponent={Link}> from "@plexui/ui/components/PlexUIProvider" (your router's Link, or "a")

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Vertically stacked panels that expand to reveal content, with one or several items open at a time and full keyboard navigation.

props.name: type
props.description: Required. Whether one item or many can be open at a time

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when the open item(s) change

props.name: collapsible
props.description: When type="single", allow closing the open item

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
const [value, setValue] = useState("shipping")
const [returnsDisabled, setReturnsDisabled] = useState(false)

<Accordion type="single" collapsible value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
<Accordion.Item value="shipping">
  <Accordion.Trigger>What are your shipping options?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>
    We offer standard (5–7 business days), express (2–3 days), and overnight shipping…
  </Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="returns" disabled={returnsDisabled}>
  <Accordion.Trigger>What is your return policy?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="support">
  <Accordion.Trigger>How can I contact customer support?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>Reach us by email, live chat, or phone Monday–Friday…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>
examples.details: The returnsDisabled control disables only the return-policy item. It remains visible and keeps its open state, while keyboard navigation skips its trigger.

examples.name: Single
examples.code:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="trial">
{items.map((item) => (
  <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
    <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
))}
</Accordion>
examples.details: Default shape. type="single" + collapsible lets users close the currently open item; without collapsible, one item is always open.

examples.name: Multiple
examples.code:
<Accordion type="multiple" defaultValue={["notifications"]}>
{items.map((item) => (
  <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
    <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
))}
</Accordion>
examples.details: Use type="multiple" when readers can keep several sections open at once: settings pages, long FAQs, step-by-step references.

<Card.Header>

<Card.Content>

components.name: Alert
components.description: Inline message for notices and warnings with semantic colors, variants, a title, a description, action slots, and a dismiss control.

props.name: actionsPlacement
props.description: Placement of actions; automatic from sizing when unset

props.name: actionsClassName
props.description: Class applied to the actions container

props.name: indicator
props.description: Custom indicator or false to hide

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows the dismiss button when set

props.name: banner
props.description: Full-width strip: square corners, lines above and below only

props.name: className
props.description: Class applied to the alert container

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Alert
title="Scheduled maintenance"
description="We'll be offline 2 - 4 AM UTC on July 14 while we upgrade our database."
actions={<Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Dismiss</Button>}
/>

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code:
<Alert
color="primary"
variant="outline"
title="Scheduled maintenance on Saturday, 2-4 AM PT"
description={<>Track status updates on <TextLink color="currentcolor" href="#">status page</TextLink></>}
/>
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the alert using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Title
examples.code: <Alert title="Your current access level limits what you can view or modify" />
examples.details: You can optionally include a title for your alert with the title prop.

examples.name: Description
examples.code:
<Alert
description={
  <>
    We're working on centralizing SCIM and invite settings. For now, setup is handled within individual product settings. <TextLink href="#">Learn more</TextLink>
  </>
}
/>
examples.details: You can optionally include description text for your alert with the description prop.

examples.name: Actions
examples.code:
<>
<Alert
  variant="soft"
  color="warning"
  title="Password expires in 3 days"
  description="Update it now to avoid losing access to your account."
  actions={<Button color="primary" pill>Update password</Button>}
/>
<Alert
  variant="soft"
  color="warning"
  title="Your API key will be rotated soon"
  description="Automatic key rotation is scheduled for March 10. Download the new key afterward to keep your integrations running."
  actions={<Button color="warning" variant="soft" pill>Remind me later</Button>}
  onDismiss={() => {}}
/>
</>
examples.details: You can add actions to the alert with the actions prop, which accepts ReactNode. Combine with onDismiss to add a dismiss button.

examples.name: Action placement
examples.code:
<Alert
title="Our terms of service has been updated"
description="We've updated our terms to clarify how we handle data, billing, and user permissions. Please review and accept the latest terms to avoid impacting your service."
actions={(
  <>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Set reminder</Button>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>Review terms</Button>
  </>
)}
actionsPlacement="bottom"
/>
examples.details: Actions are automatically positioned in the alert by default. You can force a specific position with the actionsPlacement prop by passing either 'end' or 'bottom'.

examples.name: Indicator
examples.code:
<>
<Alert
  indicator={<Lightbulb />}
  description={
    <>
      We're working on centralizing SCIM and invite settings. For now, setup is handled within individual product settings. <TextLink href="#">Learn more</TextLink>
    </>
  }
/>
<Alert
  indicator={false}
  description="Version 2.18.5 rolls out behind-the-scenes tweaks to caching and background sync. You don't need to do anything."
/>
</>
examples.details: Alert provides an indicator icon by default. You can override it by passing a custom icon to indicator, or pass indicator={'{false}'} to hide it entirely.

examples.name: Dismissible
examples.code:
<>
<Alert
  className="items-start"
  title="Try our new dashboard layout"
  description="We've introduced a streamlined layout that makes using the dashboard even easier. You can switch back any time."
  actions={(
    <>
      <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Dismiss</Button>
      <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>Try it</Button>
    </>
  )}
/>
<Alert
  title="Thank you!"
  description="Your application has been received. We will review your application and respond within the next 48 hours."
  onDismiss={() => {}}
/>
</>
examples.details: The suggested approach for dismissible notices is to use labeled buttons via actions. You can also provide onDismiss to render a dismiss button in the alert chrome.

examples.name: Banner
examples.code:
<Alert
banner
color="caution"
variant="soft"
indicator={false}
description="You are offline. Changes will sync when the connection is back."
/>
examples.details: Use banner for a full-width strip across the top or bottom of a page or panel: offline, read-only, a new version. It drops the rounded corners and keeps only the lines above and below. Pass indicator={'{false}'} for a plain strip.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description: The trail of pages that leads to the current one, above a page title, with links, plain steps and the current page.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: sm above a compact header, md above a page title

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/">Home</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/settings">Settings</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Members</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: Breadcrumb renders a nav landmark named "Breadcrumb" around an ordered list. An item with href is a link (internal paths use the linkComponent of PlexUIProvider, such as your router's link); the current item is plain text marked aria-current="page".

examples.name: Sizes
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb size="sm">
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/projects">Projects</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/projects/website">Website</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Deployments</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: Use size="sm" for a trail above a compact header; the default md sits above a page title.

examples.name: Separator
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb separator="/">
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/acme">acme</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/acme/design-system">design-system</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>README.md</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: A small chevron stands between items by default. Pass any node to separator, such as a slash for file paths. Separators are hidden from assistive technology.

examples.name: Long trails
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/">Workspace</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/accounts">Customer accounts</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/accounts/northwind">Northwind Traders</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item>Archived</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Invoice 2024-0193</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: A trail that does not fit wraps onto the next line instead of leaving the screen. An item without href is a plain step; give it onClick to make it act as a button.

props.name: href
props.description: Link destination. Internal paths use the linkComponent of PlexUIProvider

props.name: to
props.description: Router destination, for link components that take to

props.name: current
props.description: The current page: plain text marked aria-current="page"

props.name: onClick
props.description: Makes an item without a destination act as a button

components.name: Button Group
components.description: Join buttons into a single visual unit for toolbars, steppers, split buttons and search affordances.

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Go back">
    <ArrowLeftSm />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Pin</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Tag</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Bookmark</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="More options">
    <DotsHorizontal />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>

examples.name: Orientation
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom controls">
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Zoom in">
  <PlusSm />
</Button>
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Zoom out">
  <Minus />
</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Pass orientation="vertical" to stack the buttons, useful for + / − steppers, zoom controls, or any vertical toolbar. On a phone with touch.css a group of icon-only buttons keeps their 44px at each size shown, so the phone view leaves out the size control.

examples.name: Size
examples.details: Set size on every Button inside the group so corner radii match. Mix icon-only (uniform) with text buttons; each child keeps its own padding. On a phone with touch.css a group keeps one height. Beside text buttons its icon-only buttons take the heights of the iOS small (28px, sm) and medium (34px, md and lg) buttons; a group of icon-only buttons keeps their 44px, and beside a text field or a select every button takes the field's 44px. Joined segments have no iOS control of their own.

examples.name: Nested
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Pager">
<ButtonGroup>
  {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((page) => (
    <Button key={page} variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">{page}</Button>
  ))}
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Previous page">
    <ArrowLeftSm />
  </Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Next page">
    <ArrowRightSm />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Place ButtonGroup inside ButtonGroup to create visually separated sub-groups. The outer group automatically adds a small gap between children; pagination with arrow navigation is the canonical pattern.

examples.name: Separator
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm"><Undo /> Undo</Button>
<ButtonGroup.Separator />
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm">Redo <Redo /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Drop a ButtonGroup.Separator between items to add a visible divider, commonly used for Undo / Redo pairs or any "two related actions" toolbar.

examples.name: Split
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm"><Filter /> Filter</Button>
<ButtonGroup.Separator />
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Add filter">
  <Plus />
</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: The classic split button: an action joined to a secondary affordance via ButtonGroup.Separator. Useful for Save / Save-As, Filter / Add-filter, Delete / Undo.

examples.name: Input
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Input placeholder="Search docs..." size="sm" />
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" aria-label="Search">
  <SearchSm />
</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Join an Input to a trailing Button for inline search, token entry, or URL shorteners. The input flexes to fill the row; the button hugs its content. On a phone with touch.css the button takes the field's 44px at each size shown, so the phone view leaves out the size control.

examples.name: Input group
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup style={{ width: "100%", maxWidth: 280 }}>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill size="sm" uniform aria-label="Add attachment">
    <Plus />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Input
    pill
    size="sm"
    placeholder={voiceEnabled ? "Recording your idea…" : "Describe a component…"}
    disabled={voiceEnabled}
    endAdornment={
      <Input.AdornmentButton
        color={voiceEnabled ? "caution" : undefined}
        aria-label="Toggle voice mode"
        aria-pressed={voiceEnabled}
        onClick={() => setVoiceEnabled((prev) => !prev)}
      >
        <Mic />
      </Input.AdornmentButton>
    }
  />
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Richer composition for message composers: wrap each slot (leading action, flexible Input) in its own ButtonGroup so the outer group inserts a gap between them. The voice toggle rides inside the input via endAdornment. Use Input.AdornmentButton: it sizes off the input's own size token so the button stays concentric with the pill at every size. On a phone with touch.css the buttons take the field's 44px at each size shown, so the phone view leaves out the size control.

examples.name: Dropdown menu
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm">Export</Button>
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm" uniform aria-label="More export options">
      <ChevronDownMd />
    </Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={200}>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileImage /> PNG image</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileCode /> SVG vector</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileDocument /> PDF document</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Copy /> Copy as code</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Link /> Copy share link</Menu.Item>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Compose a primary action with a Menu trigger for follow-up options. Common for Export / Format, Save / Save-As, Share / ….

examples.name: Select
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Select
    options={units}
    value={unit}
    onChange={(option) => setUnit(option.value)}
    variant="outline"
    size="sm"
    block={false}
  />
  <Input placeholder="2.50" size="sm" inputMode="decimal" />
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Log weight">
    <ArrowRight />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Mix a Select and an Input inside one ButtonGroup for unit pickers, currency entry, or any "qualifier + value" pattern. Wrap each slot in a nested ButtonGroup to get a gap between the compound field and the send affordance. On a phone with touch.css the button takes the height of the 44px fields at each size shown, so the phone view leaves out the size control.

examples.name: Popover
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm"><Sparkles /> Generate</Button>
<Popover>
  <Popover.Trigger>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm" uniform aria-label="More generate options">
      <ChevronDownMd />
    </Button>
  </Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content minWidth={320} side="bottom" align="end" className="p-4">
    <Card variant="ghost" size="sm">
      <Card.Header>
        <Card.Title>Generate a component</Card.Title>
        <Card.Description>Describe what to build in plain English.</Card.Description>
      </Card.Header>
      <Card.Content>
        <Textarea placeholder="A login form with email and password…" rows={3} />
      </Card.Content>
      <Card.Footer>
        <Card.Description>Plex will draft the code and preview it live.</Card.Description>
      </Card.Footer>
    </Card>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Same split-button shape, but the trailing trigger opens a Popover instead of a menu, useful for richer panels (prompt composers, notification preferences, link previews).

components.name: Button Link
components.description: A semantic anchor with full button styling, for internal and external links with icons and block layout.

props.name: mobileMaterial
props.description: Phone surface for neutral soft/ghost buttons

props.name: disabledTone
props.description: Use relaxed visual tone for disabled state

props.name: className
props.description: Custom classes for the root element

examples.name: Overview
examples.code: <ButtonLink color="primary" pill={false} href="#">View API Keys <ArrowRight /></ButtonLink>

examples.name: Internal link
examples.code:
<ButtonLink href="/components/button" color="primary">
Internal link <ArrowRight />
</ButtonLink>
examples.details: When a relative href or to is provided, ButtonLink automatically uses the configured LinkComponent from PlexUIProvider so your router handles navigation and prefetching.

examples.name: External link
examples.code:
<ButtonLink href="#" color="primary">
External link <ArrowUpRight />
</ButtonLink>
examples.details: When linking to an external URL (or when external is set), <a> is used with target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" added automatically. If your link is not being automatically identified, you can force external link behavior with the external prop.

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.details: Stylize the link with color and variant props. On a phone the table shows the two colors of iOS buttons, accent (primary) and destructive (danger).

examples.name: Sizing & roundness
examples.code:
// Desktop
View account View account
// Phone: the three sizes of iOS buttons, small 28, medium 34 and large 50
View account View account View account

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: Field wraps a form control with a label, optional description, and error message. It automatically generates htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid linking between the label, description, error, and child control.

examples.name: With description
examples.details: Use description to display helper text below the label. The description is automatically linked to the control via aria-describedby.

examples.name: With error message
examples.details: Use errorMessage to display a validation error. When provided, the child control automatically receives aria-invalid="true". The error is rendered using the FieldError component with role="alert" for accessibility.

examples.name: Required
examples.details: Use required to show a visual asterisk after the label. This is purely visual and does not add the required HTML attribute: pass required directly to the child control for form validation.

examples.name: Sizing
examples.details: The label and description scale with the child control: Field reads the control's size, so {''} gets a lg label without repeating it. Pass size to Field to set the label size yourself, or when the child is a render prop. On a phone with touch.css a text field is 44px from 3xs to 2xl and 50px at 3xl, with the 17px text of iOS: a 3xs, 2xs or xs field takes the height, text and gutter of sm, and a horizontal label lines up with it. The phone view shows the md field and leaves out the size and pill controls, here and in the Overview; the Input page leaves them out too. In a form on a phone, put fields in rows of a FieldGroup (see Rows).

examples.name: Horizontal layout
examples.details: Use orientation="horizontal" to render the label beside the control instead of above it. On a phone with touch.css the control narrows to the width its label leaves, instead of running past the screen at its 240px (--field-horizontal-control-flex). For a form on a phone, rows are the iOS layout: see Rows below.

<Tabs variant="underline" flush value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">

<Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>

examples.details: Add flush with variant="underline" for minimal tabs where the indicator matches the text width exactly. No container border is rendered, and spacing between tabs uses gap instead of padding. On a phone these tabs are the segmented control of Overview, so this example has no Phone preview.

examples.name: Sizing
examples.code:
<Tabs variant="underline" size="md" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Demo tabs">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
examples.details: Both variants support the full 9-step size scale. The size prop controls the height, font size, icon size, and spacing of tabs. On a phone with touch.css horizontal tabs of either variant are the 32px segmented control of iOS, and vertical tabs are 52px list rows with the 17px label, at every size. The phone view shows each example at its default size, without the size and pill controls.

examples.name: Scrollable
examples.code: Overview Analytics Reports Settings Members Billing Security Integrations
examples.details: When tabs overflow their container, they automatically become horizontally scrollable. The active tab scrolls into view smoothly. No extra prop is needed: just constrain the container width.

examples.name: Overflow menu
examples.code: Code Issues Pull requests Actions Projects Insights Settings
examples.details: With overflow="menu", the tabs that do not fit stay out of the row and move into a menu at its end, instead of a sideways scroll that a phone does not show. When the active tab is a hidden one, the menu button shows its name and carries the selection. A tab's badge moves into the menu with it. overflowLabel sets the button's text (default "More"). Works for horizontal tabs without block.

components.name: Toolbar
components.description: "The top and bottom bars of a phone screen: navigation, a title, a search field and actions over the content. Desktop layouts have their own composition, so a toolbar never renders from 768px up."

props.name: placement
props.description: Top bar with 44px targets, or bottom bar with 48px targets

props.name: titleStyle
props.description: Size and place of Toolbar.Title in a top bar

props.name: titleAlign
props.description: Alignment of an inline title. Large and compact titles always start at the leading edge

props.name: background
props.description: edge fades the canvas color over the content under the bar; solid fills the bar

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <NavigationButton action="back" />
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Title>Orders</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <NavigationButton action="close" />
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
</Page>
examples.details: Leading and trailing items take 44px targets; the title is centered across the whole width. Scroll the content: the canvas color fades out over the rows under the bar, and the glass starts to cast a shadow.

examples.name: Titles
examples.code:
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
<Toolbar.Leading>
  <NavigationButton action="back" />
</Toolbar.Leading>
<Toolbar.Title subtitle="24 orders">Orders</Toolbar.Title>
<Toolbar.Trailing>
  <NavigationButton action="confirm" />
</Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
examples.details: titleStyle sets the size and place of the title: inline in the row of controls, large on a row of its own below them (on a page it scrolls up with the content under the controls, which then show it inline), and compact-large or compact-medium at the leading edge of the row. subtitle adds a second line. titleAlign="start" puts an inline title after the leading items.

examples.name: Group
examples.code:
<Toolbar>
<Toolbar.Leading>
  <NavigationButton action="close" />
</Toolbar.Leading>
<Toolbar.Trailing>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Details"><InfoCircle /></Button>
  <Toolbar.Group aria-label="Order actions">
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Translate"><Translate /></Button>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Group>
</Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
examples.details: Toolbar.Group puts related actions in one capsule. A single action keeps a capsule of its own. Name each icon button with aria-label.

examples.name: Search
examples.code:
<Toolbar>
<Toolbar.Content fill>
  <Input variant="soft" pill placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search orders" startAdornment={<Search />} />
</Toolbar.Content>
<Toolbar.Trailing>
  <NavigationButton action="close" aria-label="Close search" />
</Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
examples.details: Toolbar.Content fill stretches a search field between the leading and trailing items. The field takes the row height and the material of the bar buttons.

examples.name: Bottom
examples.code:
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Title>Orders</Toolbar.Title>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<Toolbar placement="bottom">
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Filter"><Filter /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Content>
    <Button color="primary" pill>New order</Button>
  </Toolbar.Content>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Search"><Search /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
</Page>

<Toolbar placement="bottom">
<Toolbar.Content fill>
  <Button color="primary" pill block><Plus /> New order</Button>
</Toolbar.Content>
</Toolbar>
examples.details: placement="bottom" sets the bar at the bottom of the page with 48px targets and the device's bottom safe area. Toolbar.Content centers a main action; with fill a search field or a single action takes the whole row. The page content scrolls under both bars.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.code:
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" pill>Cancel</Button>
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Title>New order</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <NavigationButton action="confirm" disabled />
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<Toolbar placement="bottom">
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Filter" disabled><Filter /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Content>
    <Button color="primary" pill disabled>Place order</Button>
  </Toolbar.Content>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Toolbar.Group aria-label="Order actions">
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Translate" disabled><Translate /></Button>
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
    </Toolbar.Group>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
</Page>
examples.details: A disabled bar button keeps its glass capsule and draws its symbol or label in the tertiary label color, as the iOS 26 bar buttons do. Inside Toolbar.Group the capsule belongs to the group, so the enabled actions next to it keep their look. A prominent action, NavigationButton action="confirm" or a solid primary Button, drops its color for a gray capsule, with a white label in light and a dim one in dark. Cancel and More stay enabled.

<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet" surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Leading>
